help.usage_examples:
Usage Examples:
• `help @` - Get help for @{string} syntax
• `help t` - Get help for t {string} syntax
• `help advert` - Get help for advert command
• `help test` - Get help for test command
• `help ping` - Get help for ping command
help.custom_syntax:
Custom Syntax:
• `t phrase` - Acknowledgment with phrase (channels & DMs)
• `@{string}` - Acknowledgment with string (DMs only)
• `advert` - Send flood advert (DMs only, 1-hour cooldown)

Location: 'here' for bot location, or lat,lon (e.g., 47.6,-122.3)
Options: radius=<nm>, alt=<min>-<max>, speed=<min>-<max>, type=<code>, callsign=<pattern>, military, limit=<n>

astronomical.sun: The Sun's AQI is off the charts! Solar wind and coronal mass ejections make Earth's air look pristine. ☀️
astronomical.moon: You like breathing regolith? The Moon has no atmosphere, so AQI is technically perfect (if you can breathe vacuum). 🌙
astronomical.the_moon: You like breathing regolith? The Moon has no atmosphere, so AQI is technically perfect (if you can breathe vacuum). 🌙
astronomical.mercury: Mercury's atmosphere is so thin it's practically vacuum. AQI: Perfect, if you can survive 800°F temperature swings. ☿️
astronomical.venus: Venus has an atmosphere of 96% CO2 with sulfuric acid clouds. AQI: Hazardous doesn't even begin to describe it. ♀️
astronomical.earth: Earth's AQI varies by location. Try a specific city or coordinates! 🌍
astronomical.mars: Mars has a thin CO2 atmosphere with dust storms. AQI: Generally good, but those dust storms are brutal. ♂️
astronomical.jupiter: Jupiter is a gas giant with no solid surface. AQI: N/A (you'd be crushed by atmospheric pressure first). ♃
astronomical.saturn: Saturn's atmosphere is mostly hydrogen and helium. AQI: Perfect, if you can survive the pressure and cold. ♄
astronomical.uranus: Uranus has methane in its atmosphere. AQI: Smells like farts, but at least it's not toxic. ♅
astronomical.neptune: Neptune's atmosphere has methane and hydrogen sulfide. AQI: Smells like rotten eggs, but you'd freeze first. ♆
astronomical.pluto: Pluto's atmosphere is mostly nitrogen with some methane. AQI: Good, but it's so cold your lungs would freeze. ♇
astronomical.europa: Europa has a thin oxygen atmosphere. AQI: Excellent, but you'd freeze solid in the vacuum of space. 🌑
astronomical.titan: Titan has a thick nitrogen atmosphere with methane. AQI: Breathable, but it's -290°F and rains liquid methane. 🪐
astronomical.io: Io has a thin sulfur dioxide atmosphere from volcanic activity. AQI: Toxic, but the radiation would kill you first. 🌋
astronomical.ganymede: Ganymede has a thin oxygen atmosphere. AQI: Good, but you'd freeze in the vacuum of space. 🛸
astronomical.callisto: Callisto has a thin carbon dioxide atmosphere. AQI: Decent, but it's -220°F and you're in space. ❄️
astronomical.enceladus: Enceladus has water vapor from geysers. AQI: Perfect, but you'd freeze instantly in space. 💧
astronomical.triton: Triton has a thin nitrogen atmosphere. AQI: Good, but it's -390°F and you're in deep space. 🥶
astronomical.space: Space has no atmosphere, so AQI is perfect! Just don't forget your spacesuit. 🚀
astronomical.void: The void of space has excellent air quality - zero pollutants! Just remember to bring your own air. 🌌
astronomical.black_hole: Black holes have no atmosphere, but the tidal forces would be a bigger problem than air quality. 🕳️
astronomical.asteroid: Asteroids have no atmosphere, so AQI is perfect! Just watch out for the vacuum of space. ☄️
astronomical.comet: Comets have thin atmospheres of water vapor and dust. AQI: Variable, but you'd freeze in space anyway. ☄️

A Siamese cat's coat darkens on its cooler extremities due to a temperature-sensitive gene. 🌡️
The Turkish Van breed is famous for actually enjoying a swim. 🏊
Cats cannot see directly beneath their own chin, so they miss food right in front of them. 🍽️
A cat's slow blink at a person is sometimes called a cat kiss and signals trust. 😌
A cat's hearing spans about 10 octaves, more than most other mammals. 🎼
Whiskers let a cat feel changes in air currents to navigate in the dark. 🌬️
Cats often knock objects off tables to test cause and effect or to get attention. 🫳
The Sphynx is not truly hairless; it is covered in a fine, peach-like down. 🍑
The Scottish Fold's folded ears come from a gene that affects cartilage body-wide. 👂
A cat's whiskers grow in four neat rows on each side of the muzzle. 🎯
The tabby pattern is named after a striped silk once made in the Attabiy district of Baghdad. 🧵
Cats have a reflective layer that makes their eyes appear to glow in photographs. ✨
A cat's rough tongue wicks saliva deep into its fur to keep the coat clean. 💧
Cats can hear the ultrasonic squeaks that mice and rats use to communicate. 🐭
A cat's pregnancy lasts roughly 63 to 65 days. 🐣
A litter of kittens is sometimes called a kindle. 🐾
House cats seek warm spots because their preferred ambient temperature is about 86 degrees F. ☀️
The first cat show in the United States was held at Madison Square Garden in 1895. 🏆
A cat's knee that appears to bend backward is actually its ankle. 🦶
The Maine Coon is among the largest domestic breeds, with some males over three feet long. 📏
A cat's outer ear has a small slit-like pocket called Henry's pocket, whose purpose is unknown. 👂
Cats often bring prey home as an instinct to provision their family or share with trusted humans. 🎁
The heaviest verified pet cat weighed nearly 47 pounds, though such records are no longer encouraged. ⚖️
